KEY MESSAGE 1...A cold front continues to sag south through the
region early this morning. A warm front lifts north through the
region tonight.

A cold front continues to sag south through the region early
this morning, and northerly winds will usher a cooler and drier
airmass into the region. Surface dew points will fall into the
40s and 50s throughout the area by this afternoon, and high
temperatures today will be much cooler than Wednesday. Highs
today will be some 15 to 20 degrees cooler than Wednesday,
topping off in the low to mid 60s.

Low pressure then develops over the Midwest today and lifts to
the northeast into the Great Lakes and Ohio Valley by this
evening, then towards the southern Province of Ontario by Friday
morning. This will pull a warm front north through the region.
Clouds will lower and thicken, and rain begins to develop late.


KEY MESSAGE 2...A strong cold frontal passage Friday evening 
will bring windy conditions, showers and potential for some 
thunderstorms, and colder temperatures into the weekend.

A sharp trough will begin shifting southeastward towards the 
region from the Upper Midwest late this week. Slow height falls 
aloft will begin across the area late Thursday night, with rapid
height falls through the day on Friday. The trough axis 
currently looks to pass through the region late Friday night or 
early Saturday morning. At the surface, a warm front will lift 
northward through the region Thursday night into Friday morning,
with a strong cold front passing through Friday evening into 
Friday night. 

Guidance continues to indicate a slower system which continues 
to delay the timing of the cold frontal passage somewhat. 
Currently, it appears likely that isentropic ascent will lead to
a broad area of mostly light showers north of the warm front 
late Thursday night into the first part of the day Friday. Once 
the region is in the warm sector, additional showers will likely
mostly hold off until the cold front approaches. 

In the warm sector, warm and moist southwesterly flow will be 
taking place with temperatures surging into the upper 70s to low
80s with dewpoints in the mid to upper 60s. Some 
destabilization is likely to take place, although the window 
will likely only be a few hours long. Guidance currently 
indicates a narrow corridor ahead of the front of around 500 
J/kg MLCAPE. While instability will be modest, wind fields aloft
will be quite strong, with 500 mb flow exceeding 60 kt. 
Scattered to widespread showers and some storms are likely to 
form along and immediately ahead of the cold front. It remains a
possibility that a few storms could become severe, with 
damaging wind gusts being the primary hazard. 

The cold front and accompanying showers and storms will clear 
the area from west to east Friday evening into Friday night. In 
the wake of the cold front, much cooler and drier air is 
expected to infiltrate the region. In addition, breezy northwest
winds look to impact the area overnight Friday night and 
through much of the day Saturday. Right now, it looks like there
could be an extended period of wind gusts in the 30-40 mph 
range, but it is not out of the question that winds could be a 
bit higher and the need for wind headlines still cannot be ruled
out. Either way, it will be a much cooler day on Saturday, with
highs only topping out in the 40s across the Poconos and far 
northern NJ, and low to mid 50s areawide. 


KEY MESSAGE 3...Widespread frost and freeze conditions are 
increasingly likely Saturday night.

Saturday night as the trough axis shifts east away from the 
region and high pressure builds in at the surface, the coldest 
air so far this season is expected across the entire area. Skies
will likely be mostly clear, with winds quickly diminishing. 
This could set the stage for very good radiational cooling 
conditions. As a result, low temperatures are expected to fall 
below freezing across the Poconos, potentially southward into 
portions of the Lehigh Valley, and adjacent areas of far 
northern NJ. For much of the rest of the area, lows in the mid 
30s to near 40 are expected. Rural areas even across 
southeastern PA and southern NJ cannot entirely rule out seeing 
their first freeze of the year. Regardless, a fairly widespread 
frost is expected across eastern PA and most of NJ, and some 
patchy frost can't be ruled out farther south into Delmarva 
either. 

Trends will continue to be monitored, but frost and/or freeze 
headlines appear increasingly likely to be needed in upcoming 
forecast cycles.
